official_sources.title: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme
official_sources.finding: JCS constrains JSON to I-JSON, rejects duplicate names, emits no insignificant whitespace, preserves array order, recursively sorts object properties and produces UTF-8 bytes suitable for repeatable hashing.
official_sources.limitation: Duplicate-name handling, IEEE-754 number limits and exact JCS number serialization must be validated by a conformant implementation; ordinary sort_keys output alone is not full JCS.

official_sources.title: Python JSON strict serialization and duplicate handling
official_sources.finding: Python json exposes sort_keys, separators, ensure_ascii, allow_nan, parse_float, parse_constant and object_pairs_hook; defaults permit NaN/Infinity and keep only the last duplicate object name.
official_sources.limitation: Python's standard encoder does not claim RFC 8785 number serialization or UTF-16 property ordering, so a JCS-specific layer and test vectors remain required.

official_sources.title: Python SHA-256 and file_digest
official_sources.finding: hashlib provides SHA-256 and file_digest for binary file hashing; digest input is bytes and weak legacy algorithms such as MD5 and SHA-1 have known collision weaknesses.
official_sources.limitation: A digest proves byte identity, not correctness, provenance, trusted acquisition or semantic equivalence.

official_sources.title: Python struct byte order, size and alignment
official_sources.finding: struct documents that native mode depends on platform and compiler alignment, while explicit little- or big-endian standard formats remove native padding and size ambiguity.
official_sources.limitation: A correct byte layout still requires the correct dtype, field meaning, shape, order and unit metadata.

official_sources.title: Python platform runtime identity
official_sources.finding: platform exposes interpreter build, compiler, architecture, system, release, machine and uname fields for a runtime fingerprint.
official_sources.limitation: Some fields can be empty, aliased, environment-dependent or insufficient to identify containers and native libraries.

official_sources.title: Python sysconfig build configuration
official_sources.finding: sysconfig exposes Python build configuration variables, installation schemes, paths, platform and interpreter version.
official_sources.limitation: Configuration variables may contain host-specific paths and differ across distributors; the captured subset and normalization rules must be explicit.

official_sources.title: Python importlib.metadata distribution identity
official_sources.finding: importlib.metadata exposes installed distribution versions, requirements, files, file sizes and recorded hashes where installation metadata supplies them.
official_sources.limitation: Import-package names are not one-to-one with distribution names, editable installs may omit metadata and files() may return None.

official_sources.title: NumPy deterministic raw-array byte order
official_sources.finding: ndarray.tobytes returns raw array bytes with an explicit C, Fortran or any-memory order; C order is the default and endian dtype is visible in reproducible examples.
official_sources.limitation: Raw bytes alone omit shape, dtype and semantic metadata; object arrays and native-endian dtypes are unsuitable for portable canonical evidence.
